st: Put the salt cod in a bowl, cover with cold water and soak for at least 4 hours or overnight, changing the water twice.
Drain the cod, put it in a pot with fresh water and boil for [[15 minutes]]. Drain, let it cool, then flake it and remove any bones.
Cut the ends off the green bananas and slit each peel lengthwise along one ridge. Do not remove the peel yet.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil with [[1 tsp]] salt. Add the bananas and boil until a knife slides in easily.
Drain the bananas and let them cool for a few minutes, then peel off the skins and cut the bananas into thick chunks.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, thyme leaves and black pepper and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the flaked cod and cook for 5 minutes, tasting before adding any extra salt because the fish is still salty.
Serve the warm banana chunks topped with the saltfish mixture.
Drain the soaked beans and rinse them well. Rinse the beef and pat it dry.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef for 6 minutes.
Add the onion, garlic and thyme and stir for 2 minutes, then pour in [[8 cups]] water.
Add the beans, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low until the beans and beef start to soften.
Mix the flour with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and about [[0.5 cup]] water to make a stiff dough. Roll small pieces into short fingers.
Add the yams, carrots and pumpkin to the pot and simmer for 15 minutes.
Drop the dumplings into the simmering soup, cover and cook for 15 minutes more until they are firm and the beans are tender.
Taste, add more salt if needed, and ladle into bowls.
Soak the salt cod in cold water for 4 hours or overnight, changing the water twice.
Drain the cod, boil it in fresh water for [[10 minutes]], then drain, cool and flake it finely, removing bones.
In a bowl mix [[1.5 cups]] flour, [[1 tsp]] baking powder and the black pepper.
Stir in the flaked cod, onion, chili, garlic and thyme leaves.
Add about [[1 cup]] cold water a little at a time until you have a thick batter that falls slowly from a spoon.
Heat [[2 cups]] oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C). A drop of batter should sizzle right away.
Fry heaping tablespoons of batter, a few at a time, for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden.
Lift the fritters out with a slotted spoon and drain them on paper towels. Serve hot.
Whisk [[3 cups]] flour, [[1 tbsp]] baking powder, [[2 tbsp]] sugar and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Rub in [[2 tbsp]] cold butter with your fingertips until the mix looks like coarse crumbs.
Add about [[1 cup]] warm water a little at a time and mix until a soft dough forms.
Knead for 3 minutes until smooth, then cover with a towel and rest for 15 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and flatten each into a disc about half an inch thick.
Heat [[2 cups]] oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the discs a few at a time for 2 to 3 minutes per side until puffed and golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with butter, cheese or saltfish.
Wash the callaloo or spinach well, remove tough stems and chop the leaves roughly. Slice the okra into rounds.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and thyme and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in [[3 cups]] broth, add the okra and the whole chili if using, and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 10 minutes until the okra is tender.
Add the greens and cook for 10 minutes until completely wilted and soft.
Remove the thyme stems and chili. Blend the soup with an immersion blender until mostly smooth.
Stir in the coconut milk, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper and heat gently for 5 minutes without boiling hard.
Taste, adjust the salt and serve hot.
Put [[1 cup]] water, the cinnamon stick and bay leaves in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes so the spices flavor the water.
Whisk [[0.25 cup]] cocoa powder with [[4 tbsp]] sugar and a pinch of salt in a small bowl.
Add a few spoonfuls of the hot spiced water to the cocoa and stir into a smooth paste.
Pour the paste into the saucepan, then add [[3 cups]] milk and stir well.
Heat gently for 5 minutes, stirring often, until steaming. Do not let it boil over.
Grate in [[0.25 tsp]] nutmeg, taste and add more sugar if you like.
Remove the cinnamon stick and bay leaves, then pour into mugs through a strainer.

ing: melted, plus extra for the pan
st: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a loaf pan with butter and line the bottom with parchment paper.
Mash the bananas in a large bowl with a fork until mostly smooth.
Stir in [[0.5 cup]] melted butter, [[0.75 cup]] sugar, the eggs and [[1 tsp]] vanilla until combined.
In another bowl whisk [[1.75 cups]] flour, [[1 tsp]] baking soda, [[0.5 tsp]] nutmeg and [[0.25 tsp]] salt.
Fold the dry mix into the banana mix until just combined. A few lumps are fine.
Pour the batter into the pan and smooth the top.
Bake for 55 to 60 minutes until a toothpick in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then lift out and cool on a rack before slicing.
